newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Dacom-KEPCO consortium wins local phone licence. [CORRECTED 08:02 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Dacom-KEPCO consortium wins local phone licence. [CORRECTED 08:02 GMT]

text.p: South Korea's information and communications ministry said on Friday it had designated a consortium led by Dacom Corp and Korea Electric Power Corp (KEPCO) as the nation's second local telephone operator.
The consortium, in which Dacom holds a 10 percent stake and Korea Electric Power Corp KEPCO seven percent, plans to begin services across the country from 1999, a Dacom official said.
Currently the local telephone services are monopolised by the state-run Korea Telecom.
Samsung Electronics Co, SK Telecom Co, Hyundai Electronics Industries Co and Daewoo Telecom Co are also members of the consortium with a six percent stake each, the Dacom official said.
The ministry also announced a third long-distance call operator (corrects from '... a third international telephone operator...') and eight other telecommunications service operators.
